mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 1 month reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are negative in > 55% of instances with FEDFUNDS decline.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% signals recessionary economic weakness, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances with UNRATE > 5.0, or signal Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth (GDPC1) > 3.0% and housing starts (HOUST) > 2000 units indicate robust consumer and construction demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Joint signal yields negative 60-day returns in > 55% of triggered cases, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year period.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion regimes, industrial production (INDPRO) above 120.0 indicates manufacturing strength, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO signal produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of early-cycle expansion instances, or regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising payroll employment level (PAYEMS) over the prior 1 month reflects labor market strength, consistently generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS trend yields negative 5-day returns in > 55% of cases, or signal Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.0% triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.0 fails to predict negative returns in > 60% of instances, or signal Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) combined with strong payroll growth (PAYEMS > 130000) signals tight labor market conditions, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Joint signal produces negative 60-day returns in > 55% of triggered cases, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, retail sales (RSAFS) above 350000 million dollars indicates sustained consumer spending strength, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: RSAFS signal yields negative 20-day returns in > 50% of late-cycle expansion instances, or regime-specific Rank IC < 0.02.
